decision_question: Does corrected semantic-target-resolution-v3 pass the unchanged grounding gates and outperform typed-target-evidence-v1 on the fixed fresh 500-case tranche?

hard_gates.name: claim-and-citation
hard_gates.evidence: Claim 91.75% and citation 93.625% are below frozen precision/recall gates.

hard_gates.name: boundary-and-safety
hard_gates.evidence: 100% boundary action and zero severe unsupported releases.

hard_gates.name: operational-completion
hard_gates.evidence: All 500 cases completed with zero operational failures.

hard_gates.name: grounded-success
hard_gates.evidence: 81.0% is below the frozen 95% gate and below the 91.0% baseline.

hard_gates.name: claim-and-citation
hard_gates.evidence: Claim 83.125% and citation 85.0% remain below frozen gates.

hard_gates.name: boundary-and-safety
hard_gates.evidence: 100% boundary action and zero severe unsupported releases.

failures.evidence: The semantic-target candidate failed full grounding on 76/400 answerable cases, concentrated in paraphrased, multi-evidence, and structured-table slices.

Even the retained baseline failed full grounding on 36/400 answerable cases despite retrieval gates passing, localizing the residual defect to semantic evidence representation and claim/citation assembly.

decision.rationale: Reject semantic-target v3, retain typed-target only as rollback, and require a source-side semantic-atom architecture on new evidence before any final or autonomy stage opens.

limitations: This is fresh development evidence rather than release confirmation.
Extractive provider-free output isolates grounding architecture.
No professor fidelity, real usability, learning outcome, visual, or provider-backed autonomy claim is supported.
